note: Rav Naḥman and Rabbi Yitzḥak sat at a meal. Rav Naḥman asked for a teaching; Rabbi Yitzḥak said one may not talk while eating, lest one choke. After the meal he taught, in Rabbi Yoḥanan's name, that Jacob our father did not die. Rav Naḥman asked whether he was eulogized, embalmed and buried for nothing; Rabbi Yitzḥak said he was interpreting a verse. He also said anyone who says 'Rahab, Rahab' at once has a seminal emission; Rav Naḥman said it did not affect him, and Rabbi Yitzḥak said he meant those who knew her. Parting, Rav Naḥman asked for a blessing. Rabbi Yitzḥak told of a traveler who blessed a tree that its saplings be like it, and blessed him: may your offspring be like you.

people.name: Rav Naḥman
people.about: Shares a meal with Rabbi Yitzḥak and asks him for teachings and a blessing

people.name: Rabbi Yitzḥak
people.about: Teaches Rav Naḥman and blesses him when they part

people.name: Rabbi Yoḥanan
people.about: Sage in whose name Rabbi Yitzḥak teaches

terms.meaning: Jacob, the biblical father of the twelve tribes of Israel.
A woman of Jericho in the Bible, described here as so beautiful that her name alone aroused desire.
A short illustrative story used to make a point.

note: Ilfa and Rabbi Yoḥanan studied Torah together and grew very poor, so they set out to go into business. Sitting under a crumbling wall eating bread, Rabbi Yoḥanan heard two ministering angels: one wanted to knock the wall down and kill them for leaving eternal life for passing life; the other said to leave them, since one had his time still ahead. Ilfa heard nothing, so Rabbi Yoḥanan concluded the future was his and went back. Ilfa went on, and by his return Rabbi Yoḥanan led the academy. Told he too would have led had he stayed, Ilfa hung from a ship's mast, vowing to fall and drown if he could not answer any question on certain baraitot from the Mishna. An old man posed a case about a will, and Ilfa answered.
why: The Gemara presents this as another story involving an unstable wall, and follows it with one about a house that collapses the moment Naḥum of Gam Zu is carried out.

people.name: Ilfa
people.about: Rabbi Yoḥanan's study partner, who goes into business and later proves his learning

people.name: Rabbi Yoḥanan
people.about: Hears the angels, returns to study, and becomes head of the academy

terms.meaning: Angels who serve God; here two of them debate whether to kill the two men.
A teaching of the early Sages not included in the Mishna; Ilfa offers to explain those of Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Oshaya.
The early code of Jewish law the Talmud discusses.
Coins; the text says a sela is double a shekel.

note: Most of Adar had passed with no rain, and the people asked Ḥoni HaMe'aggel to pray. He prayed, and no rain fell. He drew a circle, stood in it, and swore by God's name not to move until God had mercy on His children. Rain trickled; he asked for rain to fill the cisterns, and it poured in huge drops; he asked for rain of blessing, and it fell normally until the people fled to the Temple Mount. Asked to pray it away, he said one does not pray over too much good, yet he offered a thanks-offering bull and prayed, and the sun came out. Shimon ben Shetaḥ sent word that he would have excommunicated him, were he not Ḥoni, who nags God like a son his father and gets his way.
why: The mishna mentioned in passing that the people sent to Ḥoni for rain; the Gemara now gives the full account, after discussing rain that comes in its season and sin that holds it back.

people.name: Ḥoni HaMe'aggel
people.about: Draws a circle and will not leave it until God sends rain

people.name: Shimon ben Shetaḥ
people.about: Sage who rebukes Ḥoni but cannot punish him

terms.meaning: A Hebrew month near the end of winter, late for rain to begin.
A small liquid measure; the Sages judged no raindrop was smaller than one.
A sacrifice brought to thank God.
A formal ban by the Sages cutting a person off from the community.

note: Rav taught that each day a heavenly voice proclaims that the whole world is fed for the sake of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa, yet he lives on a kav of carobs from one Shabbat eve to the next. Every Friday his wife heated the oven and made smoke, out of embarrassment, so no one would know they had nothing to bake. A malicious neighbor, suspicious, knocked on the door, and the embarrassed wife went into an inner room. A miracle happened: the neighbor saw the oven full of bread and the kneading basin full of dough, and called to her to bring a shovel before her bread burned. The wife answered that she had gone in for just that, and a tanna taught that she was used to miracles.
why: The Gemara has just told how Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa's prayers stopped and restarted the rain, and continues with more wonders done for him and his family.

people.name: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa
people.about: A righteous man for whose sake the world is fed, though he lives on almost nothing

people.name: Rav
people.about: Teaches about the heavenly voice, as reported by Rav Yehuda

terms.meaning: A voice from heaven announcing God's word.
A small measure of volume; a kav of carobs is a meager amount of poor food.
A Sage of the early period whose teachings are quoted in the Talmud.

note: Of the twenty-four families of priests who took turns serving in the Temple, only four came back from the exile in Babylonia: Jedaiah, Harim, Pashhur and Immer. The prophets among the returnees divided these four into twenty-four new watches by drawing lots from a receptacle, each of the four families drawing its own lot and five more. The prophets also stipulated that if the family of Jehoiarib, which had originally headed the watches, ever returned, Jedaiah would keep first place and Jehoiarib would be subordinate to it.
why: The Gemara has been asking how Moses first set up the priestly watches, whether sixteen or eight, and how they grew to twenty-four; this teaching of the Sages carries the same question forward to how the twenty-four were rebuilt after the exile.

people.name: Jedaiah
people.about: One of the four priestly families that returned from exile; it was given first place among the watches.

people.name: Harim
people.about: One of the four priestly families that returned from exile.

people.name: Pashhur
people.about: One of the four priestly families that returned from exile.

people.name: Immer
people.about: One of the four priestly families that returned from exile.

people.name: Jehoiarib
people.about: The priestly family that originally headed the watches; it did not return, and would rank below Jedaiah if it did.

terms.meaning: The priests were divided into groups, each serving in the Temple for its own week in rotation.
The period after the First Temple was destroyed, when much of the Jewish people lived in Babylonia; some later returned to the Land of Israel.
